prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses on Loans
prov.text:
The following table sets forth information regarding our provisions for credit losses on loans, charge-offs and recoveries and ending allowance for credit losses for loans at the dates and for the periods indicated:

Managing high-risk credits includes developing a business strategy with the customer to mitigate our potential losses. Management continues to monitor these credits with a view to identifying as early as possible when, and to what extent, additional provisions may be necessary. Management believes that the level of allowance for credit losses has been adjusted accordingly.

During the third quarter of 2026, the Company recorded net loan charge-offs of $1,377,000 compared to net recoveries of $75,000 for the same period in 2025. The primary reason for loan charge-offs during the quarter was for charge-offs within an acquired student loan portfolio from the Merger, in which the Company recorded a Day 1 allowance of $8.4 million in anticipation of future charge-offs in this portfolio segment. The net charge-off ratio reflects annualized net charge-offs to average loans of 0.15% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to annualized net recoveries of 0.01% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.heading: Non-Interest Expenses
nonint.text:
The following table shows significant components of non-interest expense for the periods indicated:

Salaries and employee benefits, occupancy and equipment, information technology, data processing, professional services,

acquisition and integration expenses, and regulatory assessments are the major categories of non-interest expenses.

Non-interest expenses increased $24,001,000 or 108.27% to $46,168,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $22,167,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The net increase for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily the result of merger expenses of $7,167,000, an expense incurred as a result of a one-time legal settlement of $6,615,000, increases in salaries and employee benefits of $4,142,000, amortization of core deposit intangibles of $1,624,000, occupancy and equipment of $1,025,000, and information technology of $964,000. The legal settlement resolved ongoing litigation related to a former depositor. The increase in expenses for the quarter-to-date period was primarily driven by the Merger.

Non-interest expenses increased $40,364,000 or 59.42% to $108,298,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $67,934,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

pretax.text: Net interest income before the provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $18,400,000 or 52.66% to $53,344,000 compared to $34,944,000 for the same period in 2025. The increase was a result of increased interest income on average earning assets and a decrease in interest expense on average interest bearing liabilities.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text:
Our effective income tax rate was 28.48% and 27.88% for the three month periods ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The increase in the effective tax rate was primarily driven by non-deductible expenses incurred in connection with the Merger. Our effective income tax rate was 28.59% and 27.42% for the nine month periods ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.

The Company reported an income tax provision of $3,212,000 and $4,203,000 for the three month periods ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The Company reported an income tax provision of $8,906,000 and $10,201,000 for the nine month periods ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

The Company recognizes accrued interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits as a component of tax expense in the consolidated statements of income. If deemed necessary, the Company maintains a reserve for uncertain income taxes where the merits of the position taken or the amount of the position that would be ultimately sustained upon examination do not meet a more-likely-than-not criteria. As of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, there was no reserve for uncertain tax positions.

On June 27, 2025, California Senate Bill 132 (“SB 132”) was passed and signed into law by Governor Newsom. Effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, SB 132 amends California Rev. & Tax.

net.text: • Net income during the third quarter increased to $8.07 million, or $0.30 per diluted common share, compared to net income of $2.70 million and $0.10 per diluted common share, respectively, in the second quarter of 2026.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin
Net interest income.text:
The level of net interest income depends on several factors in combination, including yields on earning assets, the cost of interest-bearing liabilities, the relative volumes of earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, and the mix of products which comprise the Company’s earning assets, deposits, and other interest-bearing liabilities. To maintain its net interest margin, the Company must manage the relationship between interest earned and paid.

The following Distribution, Rate and Yield table presents the average amounts outstanding for the major categories of the Company’s balance sheet, the average interest rates earned or paid thereon, and the resulting net interest margin on average interest earning assets for the periods indicated. Average balances are based on daily averages.

intro.text: Effective on April 1, 2026, Community West Bancshares completed its merger with United Security Bancshares, with Community West Bancshares continuing as the surviving entity. Shortly thereafter United Security Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary of United Security Bancshares, merged with and into Community West Bank, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Community West Bancshares, with Community West Bank continuing as the surviving banking institution. Pursuant to the terms of the merger agreement, each share of United Security Bancshares common stock was converted into the right to receive 0.4520 shares of Community West Bancshares common stock, with cash to be paid in lieu of any fractional shares.
